newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish yields end higher on German rate fears.
newsitem.headline: Swedish yields end higher on German rate fears.

text.p: Swedish debt yields rose and the crown softened under the pressure from comments made by German institutes that German rates may rise.
However, better than expected economic data from the U.S. succeeded in reversing the rise in late trade, and dealers expect the market to continue to firm on Wednesday.
"It will probably fall further in early trade tomorrow," one dealer said.
Nine-year debt yields ended Tuesday four basis points higher at 7.23 percent. Four-year debt yields also climbed four basis points to 5.94 percent.

The crown fell to 4.3430 against the German mark compared to 4.3260 crowns late on Tuesday. The Swedish currency bottomed out at around 4.3500 against the mark before the Riksbank intervened and bought crowns.
Analysts agree that the Riksbank has a target for the crown. Some say the Riksbank's aim is a narrow range around 4.30 against the German mark. Others believe the Riksbank's target is less tight.
